findings.finding: The plan cites the synchronous push-path URL resolution as `push.py:418` (`remote_url = _git(base_path, "remote", "get-url", remote)`), but that resolution is actually at line 455; line 418 currently sits inside the async `Popen` argument list. findings.finding: Because the S3 preflight is placed inside push_tickets_branch, the consumer push_after_commit (src/rebar/_store/push.py:659-664) wraps the call in a bare `except Exception:` that logs and returns — it would SWALLOW the OptionalDependencyError, so the inline-commit write paths it feeds (transition/reopen/claim in txn.py, compact, delete) would NOT fail closed on a missing/too-old S3 helper. This consumer is outside the plan's enumerated call sites (which name only write_and_push at event_append.py:587) and its swallow defeats the fail-closed intent for those paths.
findings.location: Approach — 'The best-effort contract, resolved explicitly' / src/rebar/_store/push.py:659-664 (push_after_commit)
findings.suggested_fix: Let OptionalDependencyError escape push_after_commit's except (re-raise it, or run the preflight before entering the swallowing try), so the inline-commit write paths halt with the actionable message like write_and_push does.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Cite git-remote-s3's documented URL schemes (docs/--help) to confirm s3:// and s3+zip:// are the COMPLETE set that must trigger the S3 preflight, so no accepted S3 URL form fails open past the prefix check.
evidence: Plan quote: 'iff its resolved URL starts with `s3://` or `s3+zip://` (git-remote-s3's own schemes)'

Evidence class: Partially-verified — the internal seam require_s3_helper() is landed and confirmed (src/rebar/_optional.py), but the completeness of the S3 URL scheme set is an external-capability claim not verified against git-remote-s3 docs/--help; resolve_symbol('git_remote_s3') returned UNRESOLVED (not proof either way).
Impact is directional: a missed S3 scheme fails OPEN (unlocked push -> store corruption), which is the failure mode the story targets.
findings.finding: The plan asserts s3:// and s3+zip:// are 'git-remote-s3's own schemes' and treats that pair as the complete set of URL prefixes that put the store in S3 mode, but does not ground the scheme list against the helper's documentation/--help. The load-bearing correctness of the fail-closed guard depends on this set being complete: any additional S3 URL form the helper accepts but the prefix check omits would fail OPEN, driving the exact unlocked push the story exists to prevent.
findings.location: Approach: 'Treat a remote as S3 mode iff its resolved URL starts with s3:// or s3+zip:// (git-remote-s3's own schemes).'
scenarios: An operator configures sync.remote with an S3 URL form accepted by git-remote-s3 but not matching the s3://|s3+zip:// prefixes (e.g. an alternate/aliased scheme), so the preflight is a no-op and the unlocked push proceeds.

The plan enumerates only write_and_push (which does NOT catch) and never mentions push_after_commit.
findings.location: Approach / 'The best-effort contract, resolved explicitly.'; push.py:646-668 push_after_commit
findings.suggested_fix: Either let push_after_commit re-raise OptionalDependencyError (catch it specifically before the broad except and re-raise), or run _require_s3_helper_if_s3_url on the resolved remote before entering push_after_commit's try; and add these inline-commit paths to the scope + test oracles.
